cases.description: Create a valid METHODOLOGY.md from sufficient upstream intent and observed workflow evidence.
expected: Answers the primary methodology question
Defines stages, validation loops, and feedback cycles
Distinguishes durable method from tactical scheduling
Passes specification acceptance criteria

cases.description: Observed practice and stated process conflict, or the workflow evidence is incomplete.
expected: Does not invent a coherent method
Labels assumptions and contradictions
Reports blocked or provisional completion
Requests the missing or resolving evidence

cases.description: An existing METHODOLOGY.md must be updated after the team changed how validation and feedback loops operate.
expected: Updates the affected workflow stages or loops
Retains still-valid durable method
Revalidates human and AI collaboration guidance
Reports downstream automation or docs needing review

cases.description: Input material collapses methodology into a backlog, CI YAML, or release checklist.
expected: Identifies the boundary violation
Keeps tactical planning and implementation detail out of the canonical document
Explains the correct owning artifact
Produces a safe methodology-focused revision or follow-up

cases.description: The real need is only to schedule roadmap work or edit a CI workflow without changing the operating model.
expected: Declines to use this skill as the primary tool
Directs the work toward roadmap or automation changes instead
Avoids treating tooling edits as methodology by default
Explains why the trigger is negative
